subject: Priority triage: orphaned/opps re-engagement and SFDC commit clarity
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority triage: orphaned/opps re-engagement and SFDC commit clarity

Team —

Quick pulse on a tiny but high-risk set: Finance flagged a small cluster of opportunities in our Q4 forecast that are >90 days without stage movement but still in commit (Forecast Category: Commit). That mismatch is creating noise in the forecast and inflating our expected revenue for the month.

I attached a skinny extract (20261005-orphan-list-MediCore.csv) showing the top 12 deals by ARR where owner is blank or listed as a non-responder. Please do the following by EOD tomorrow:

- Owners: claim any deals you are actively working on and update "Owner" and "Next Step" in SFDC.
- If not actively working: change Stage to "Shelved" or move to Closed/Lost as appropriate and add a short note with the reason.
- For true commit deals: set a clear close-by date (no open-ended "TBD") and confirm the evidence (PO, procurement cadence, signed SOW) in the Deal Notes.

Why this matters: finance needs a cleaned commit set for the 10/08 revenue cut. Leaving old/opportunistic deals in commit skews our capacity planning with Dedicated nodes and impacts the Q4 cadence for rounding.

Attachments: 20261005-orphan-list-MediCore.csv, commit-criteria-checklist.pdf

Reference: hubspot record linked here — https://hubspot.company/record/DEAL-MEDCORE-42

Thanks — small focused effort here will save us a major reconciliation headache.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
(Attachment: 20261005-orphan-list-MediCore.csv)
